{"id":"bdacca50-b604-40c7-b2c1-138868563e74","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510254,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"parent_requirement_id":"R3","mode":"residual","used_claims":["C1"],"local_residual":"Whether a partner of the artist at the time of the artist's death gave an interview in which the partner said that, following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist's songs."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer only JSON object. Parent req: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." Need find what still needs established. C1 supports artist = Sophie? It establishes Sophie death, accidental, city Athens. Does not establish partner interview, or statement that following death artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. So residual: identify partner at time of death of the artist and whether they gave an interview stating after artist's death, artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs. But must choose exactly ONE coherent evidence objective. Could be "the artist's partner at the time of death gave an interview in which they said that after the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." This is one objective. Need preserve roles, relation. Since C1 used for artist. used_claims ["C1"] because supports identity/death? Parent Requirement mentions artist's death. C1 establishes death? It says Sophie died. It supports artist. We can use C1. local_residual should be not search query. It can mention "Whether the partner... gave an interview..." Maybe mode residual.

Need ensure no adding "Sophie" if not in Parent? C1 identifies artist as Sophie. We can mention artist (Sophie). Parent requirement says partner of artist at time of death. C1 only established artist died. Partner not established. Need local residual: "Whether the artist's partner at the time of the artist's death gave an interview in which the partner said that following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist's songs." That's coherent. It bundles partner and interview and quote? Actually it is one relation: partner gave interview containing statement. But maybe too bundled? The parent requirement contains a single complex relation: partner gave interview + content. We can formulate exactly.

Maybe if partner unknown, objective is "Identify the artist's partner at the time of the artist's death and establish whether that partner gave an interview stating..." That's two? But to establish parent requirement, need both. However guideline: choose exactly ONE coherent part, not bundle independent. The partner and interview are not independent? The parent requirement itself is one semantic condition involving partner. The current evidence context has only C1. No part of R3 supported. We can choose low-commitment facet: "the identity of the artist's partner at the time of the artist's death." But parent requirement specifically is about interview statement, not just partner identity. If no substantive part of Parent supported, still choose one faithful low-commitment facet. The facet "the identity of the partner at time of death" is part, but is it inside Parent? It is presupposed. But the core relation is partner gave interview. Maybe better to target the interview statement. Since partner identity unknown, but can research "whether any partner of the artist gave an interview..." Hmm.

Need output JSON only.

Let's craft:

{
 "parent_requirement_id": "R3",
 "mode": "residual",
 "used_claims": ["C1"],
 "local_residual": "Whether the artist's partner at the time of the artist's death gave an interview in which the partner stated that, following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist's songs."
}

Would "at time of death" and "following death" preserved. Song unspecified. No downstream title. Good.

But maybe C1 shouldn't be used because it establishes death but not the parent? It is supporting Claim relevant. The schema used_claims. If no substantive supporting Claim for parent, use mode probe and used_claims []. Is C1 substantive supporting? It establishes artist identity/death but not R3. However parent requirement involves "artist's death" context. C1 says Sophie died accidental. It is part of original but not R3 except "their death". R3 relies on artist and death. C1 supports that. So residual mode okay with C1.

Need maybe local_residual: "The identity of the partner (at the time of the artist's death) and whether that partner gave an interview saying that following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." But identity + whether interview is two? Maybe phrase as "whether the artist's partner ... gave..." includes identification as part. But if partner unknown, the objective is to establish the existence of such partner/interview. We can say "Establish whether a partner of the artist at the time of the artist's death gave an interview..." That doesn't require prior identity. Good.
